claims.claim: The Tax Code (Sec. 23) taxes an alien, resident or not, only on Philippine-source income, so US dividends, interest, gains and loan draws are untaxed locally

sources.name: ChanRobles: National Internal Revenue Code, Sec. 23
sources.says: Section 23(D): "An alien individual, whether a resident or not of the Philippines," "is taxable only on income derived from sources within the Philippines;".

sources.name: PwC: Philippines, taxes on personal income
sources.says: Last reviewed 02 July 2026. Non-resident citizens and aliens are "taxed only on income from sources within the Philippines"; resident citizens on worldwide income. The page does not state the scope for resident aliens.

claims.note: The statute is read on ChanRobles' copy, not a government site; the BIR's pages carry no text on it. PwC confirms it for non-resident aliens and is silent on resident aliens.

sources.says: Last reviewed 02 July 2026. "Dividend income received from a domestic corporation is taxed at 10% for resident aliens"; "Philippine-source interest and royalties are taxed at 20%"; some FCDU interest 15%.

claims.claim: A flat 6% estate tax on the net estate, after a PHP 5m standard deduction and up to PHP 10m for the family home

sources.name: Respicio & Co.: estate tax computation in the Philippines
sources.says: Dated January 12, 2026. "Under the TRAIN Law, the estate tax is a flat 6% on the net estate"; standard deduction "PHP 5,000,000 (fixed under TRAIN Law)"; family home up to PHP 10 million; the tax applies to "The worldwide estate of Filipino citizens and resident aliens", and for non-resident aliens to "Only properties situated in the Philippines".

sources.name: PwC: quick chart, inheritance and gift tax rates
sources.says: Thailand (24 August 2026): inheritance 10, gift 5; Malaysia (16 June 2026): NA, NA; Vietnam (23 September 2026): 10, 10; Indonesia (11 June 2026): NA, NA; Philippines (01 August 2026): "There is no inheritance tax in the Philippines." "an estate tax of 6% is imposed on the assets of the decedent taxpayer."

claims.note: The BIR's estate-tax page (bir.gov.ph/estate-tax) loaded with only its heading.
claims.modelMismatch: localTaxes.ts (PH) models the 6% after the PHP 5m standard deduction only; the family-home deduction (up to PHP 10m) is not modelled. For stage 8 to judge; it overstates the tax only where the family home is in the estate.
claims.notModelled: The family-home deduction (up to PHP 10m) is not applied: the modelled estate is the portfolio, with no home in it, so the 6% after PHP 5m stands. The PH note says so.

claims.claim: US estate tax applies above the $15M exemption (2026): "the $15M US exemption (2026) applies as anywhere"

sources.name: IRS: What's new, estate and gift tax
sources.says: The table "Basic exclusion amount for year of death" has the row 2026: $15,000,000 (2025: $13,990,000). The page says the Working Families Tax Cuts, Public Law 119-21, signed July 4, 2025, "amends § 2010(c)(3) by increasing the basic exclusion amount to $15,000,000 for calendar year 2026". Page last reviewed or updated 03-Nov-2026.

sources.name: IRS: Estate tax
sources.says: A return is required when the gross estate, plus adjusted taxable gifts and specific exemption, is more than the filing threshold for the year of death; the table gives 2026: $15,000,000. Page last reviewed or updated 23-Oct-2026.

sources.name: IRS news release IR-2025-103: tax inflation adjustments for tax year 2026
sources.says: "Estates of decedents who die during 2026 have a basic exclusion amount of $15,000,000", up from $13,990,000 for 2025; the release (October 9, 2025) cites Revenue Procedure 2025-32 and is marked as an archival document.

sources.name: IRS: Some nonresidents with U.S. assets must file estate tax returns
sources.says: "U.S. citizens are subject to U.S. estate taxation with respect to their worldwide assets"; Form 706 is required when worldwide assets plus adjusted taxable gifts exceed the basic exclusion amount in effect on the date of death. By contrast a nonresident who is not a citizen files when US-situated assets exceed $60,000. Page last reviewed or updated 27-Jun-2026.
